"would_settle": "OpenAI publishing its completed model-behaviour review with a list of affected organisations and dates, or the Australian Signals Directorate publishing its forensic findings.",
"settled": null
+      "question": "Will any of the four proceedings opened this week produce a finding of liability against an AI developer?",

+      "would_settle": "A civil investigative demand served and reported, a docket number for the LASST case, a bill number and committee referral for the AI Agent Accountability Act, or a court order on the injunction LASST seeks."

"The defenders' side of the record hardened and hedged in the same week. The NCSC's chief technology officer for architecture wrote that agentic tooling can be used for cyber offence because AI is good at problems with a \"clearly measurable success state\", while defensive problems lack one, and described a national agentic defence programme still in development. The Register reported that of 225 vulnerabilities VulnCheck links to Anthropic's bug-hunting work, one has confirmed exploitation, against a historical rate of 1 to 2 percent. KEX-bench put the strongest coding agent at 56.0% of Linux kernel-exploit tasks and 5.0% of Windows tasks. Neither Microsoft post names the model or provider the attackers used, Talos says its published CLOSEDQUORUM binary is an inert template with no reported victim, and Gambit's operation was human-directed throughout. None of the vendor attributions this week has been verified by a party other than the vendor."

"changed": "The arc gained its first law-enforcement outcome — 50 sites seized and two arrests over an AI phishing platform — and its first recovered attacker infrastructure, which put a per-target cost on agent-driven intrusion. On the defensive side the UK's NCSC stated plainly that agentic tooling favours offence, and the count of Anthropic-linked CVEs actually exploited stayed at one."
+      "text": [

+        "As of 5 October the largest vendor in the field has put its judgement in writing: attackers are reaching AI advantages before defenders. Microsoft's 2026 Digital Defense Report, published 1 October, states that Mythos and GPT-5.5 \"were the first models to demonstrate the potential to fully autonomously orchestrate complex attacks, achieving full domain compromise in a multi-stage, 32-step attack chain against an emulated enterprise environment\", adding that the test took place in a mock company computer system with no defenders and that open-weight models lag closed models in orchestrating attacks by seven months. Its incident-response findings put phishing at 23% of initial access against 7% a year earlier, and exploitation of public-facing applications at 24% against 15%. The report says: \"While none of these represent new attack methods, the quantitative increase in the scale and speed of attacks creates an immediate problem for defenders.\"",

+        "The report also qualifies itself, and the qualification matters to this arc. On identity it says \"most of what we exploit there has nothing to do with AI\", and separate telemetry inside the same document puts phishing at a much lower share of intrusion attempts than the incident-response findings do. Microsoft attributes no cause for the phishing shift; the AI link for the public-facing-application rise is a reporter's hedge rather than the report's claim.",

+        "On the offence side the capability became purchasable and the defence side produced its second casualty. Anthropic reported that Zhipu's GLM-5.3 developed end-to-end exploits in 50 of 410 attempts, that its safeguards were bypassed between 64% and 100% of the time with simple techniques, and called the release \"a meaningful step change in the cyber capabilities available to attackers\". Google's threat group reported that half of the vulnerabilities it judges likely to have been AI-discovered enable remote code execution, against 26% of the rest. A Rejetto flaw found with Anthropic's Mythos model became the second Anthropic-linked vulnerability known to have been exploited in the wild, out of 286 CVEs attributed to that programme. No government body, CERT or second vendor published comparable counts or verified any vendor AI attribution this week; CISA added two exploited Zammad flaws to its catalogue on 2 October, and its alert makes no reference to AI."

+      "changed": "Microsoft moved the arc's central claim from inference to a published vendor judgement, with a 32-step fully autonomous domain compromise and a near-tripling of phishing's share of initial access — while qualifying in the same report that most identity exploitation has nothing to do with AI. The verification question stayed open: CISA confirmed the Zammad flaws are exploited but said nothing about AI."

"The one place rules were being written, they were removed. The Washington Post reported that US and Russian diplomats worked to weaken a UN draft framework on AI weapons this month, stripping a requirement that humans review AI-generated targets. At the General Assembly the Secretary-General said in the same week that \"life-and-death decisions must never be surrendered to machines\" and that \"Killer robots must have no place in our future\", and at the White House Xi Jinping said the two countries have both the capability and responsibility to ensure that the development of AI is always under human control. Neither the removal nor the statements changes any published procurement document. No government has published rules for autonomous target selection, and the question this storyline tracks is unanswered in the same week its deployment figures grew."

"changed": "The deployment side produced its first user and target counts at scale — Maven past 100,000 users and 13,000 targets in 38 days — while the Washington Post reported that the human-review requirement was stripped from the UN draft framework. No government has published rules for autonomous target selection."
+      "text": [

+        "As of 5 October the United States is building an institution for autonomous warfare and has still published no rules for autonomous target selection. At Marine Corps Base Quantico on 30 September Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced \"a new four-star combatant command with service-like authorities built to scale autonomous and robotic capabilities across the joint force\", with a memo released after the speech setting stand-up by 1 October 2027. Reporting on the budget request behind it puts the fiscal 2027 ask for the Defense Autonomous Warfare Group at $54.6 billion, against about $226 million the year before, and describes a memorandum titled \"Project Agincourt: Pathway to the Autonomous Warfare Command\" signed the same day and requiring a plan of action and milestones within 30 days. Hegseth is quoted calling drone warfare combined with \"SI-enabled targeting\" \"the biggest battlefield revolution in generations\".",

+        "The institution-building continued through the week. Breaking Defense reported that the Pentagon is turning its autonomy portfolio office into Project Agincourt as an interim step toward standing up the command. The Defense Innovation Unit's director took leave to help bring the command into fruition through Project Agincourt, reporting directly to Hegseth, and the Army established a Futures and Autonomous Systems Command with a new acquisition executive for autonomy and a deadline of no later than fiscal 2028 to acquire and field autonomous systems.",

+        "What has not appeared is any of the material this storyline tracks. No published autonomy test data, evaluation results or rules of engagement for target selection accompanied the announcement, the memorandum as reported, the Army's memo, or the counter-drone awards made the day before, and DefenseScoop reported that no AI or autonomy is attributed to any awarded system. The command is contingent on Congress. Northrop Grumman reported a first fully autonomous flight of its YFQ-48A Talon Blue on 3 October, from taxi through landing; no source connects that flight to the new command. NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe is reported to be presenting a document titled \"Theory of Victory\" in Poland on 12 October, built in part on AI-powered targeting; it has not been published."

+      "changed": "The arc gained a budget line and a chain of command: a four-star Autonomous Warfare Command with a 1 October 2027 stand-up date, an interim Project Agincourt, a new Army autonomy command, and a fiscal 2027 request reported at $54.6 billion against about $226 million the year before. No government has published rules for autonomous target selection, and none of the week's documents included autonomy test data."

"Chips stayed outside the arrangement. The US Trade Representative said export controls on advanced chips and chipmaking equipment were not on the agenda, and Trump said afterwards that the United States is not going to be putting on brakes. Roll Call reported that Senate Armed Services Chairman Roger Wicker agreed to fold Senator Tom Cotton's chip location-tracking bill into the managers amendment to the fiscal 2027 defence authorisation, alongside bills from Senators Pete Ricketts and Jim Banks, with House Foreign Affairs Committee counterparts already reported out; none has passed either chamber and Senate Democrats blocked the authorisation over unrelated objections. On the domestic-supply side Alibaba unveiled the Zhenwu V900 accelerator and set a target of more than 20GW of data-centre capacity by 2032. No named Chinese company has produced records contradicting the distillation figures, and no US agency has published its own analysis."

"changed": "The AI dialogue Washington proposed a week earlier was agreed at the state visit and given a date, but the two readouts name it differently and neither publishes a threshold or an agency. Chip export controls were explicitly kept off the summit agenda while three export-control bills were folded into a defence authorisation that remains blocked."

+        "As of 5 October the substitution case and the enforcement case were both made in public, and neither was made with numbers that can be checked. Huawei chairman Eric Xu claimed on 30 September that Ascend had exceeded Nvidia in Chinese market share — \"It's pretty hard to collect data about the market share of Nvidia in China, but based on the data we have collected, Ascend has surpassed Nvidia\" — and said \"Even though our chips may be less advanced, at least their supply is assured\". Huawei published no sales figure. Xu also said the company does not have enough capacity to satisfy demand in China and has no plans to expand the international market in a fully-fledged way, and two days later a second Huawei executive said advanced-semiconductor capacity in China \"is indeed limited\", that Ascend chips use that capacity, and that on lithography \"right now we're still relying on DUV domestically\".",

+        "The software layer moved in Huawei's direction the same day. DeepSeek open-sourced six software modules tailored for Ascend chips, mirroring its prior open-source tools for Nvidia's, toward an \"independent and controllable\" ecosystem. A Washington research group estimated that Chinese-owned fabs imported 343 immersion DUV systems by the first quarter of 2026 and urged a total ban, tying the tools to Huawei in a section headed on the permitted entry of ASML's NXT:1980i despite its enabling production of Ascend AI chips at scale. Reuters, citing the Financial Times, reported Tencent had signed to lease about 100,000 AI chips from Oracle. OpenAI said it disrupted a model-distillation campaign whose core cluster it links to Moonshot AI, identifying related activity across more than 15,000 users. No named Chinese company has produced records contradicting the distillation figures, and no source connected the smuggling prosecution to the lithography estimate or to Huawei's claims."
